messages:
maria: Quick FYI — we plan to run the RBAC roles schema refactor in staging tonight 22:00 UTC. This is the migration that adds canonical_role, backfills user_role mappings, and sets safe defaults. Need oncall + infra aware.

kevin: What are the exact safe defaults? will legacy role strings be remapped 1:1 or collapsed?

maria: Plan is to collapse noisy legacy variants into canonical categories (admin, engineer, reviewer, viewer, service). Legacy mappings in the migration are explicitly defined so it's deterministic. Default fallback is 'viewer' unless a service flag exists.

alyssa: Sharing the SQL we'll run in staging first (batched):

```sql
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE roles ADD COLUMN canonical_role VARCHAR(64) DEFAULT NULL;
UPDATE roles SET canonical_role = CASE
  WHEN name ILIKE 'admin_%' THEN 'admin'
  WHEN name ILIKE 'eng_%' OR name ILIKE 'engineer%' THEN 'engineer'
  WHEN name ILIKE 'svc_%' THEN 'service'
  ELSE 'viewer'
END;
-- backfill user_role mappings in small batches to avoid locking
INSERT INTO user_roles (user_id, role, source)
SELECT u.id, r.canonical_role, 'migration_2024_03' FROM users u
JOIN roles r ON u.role_id = r.id
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_roles ur WHERE ur.user_id = u.id AND ur.source = 'migration_2024_03');
COMMIT;
```

samir: Two operational notes: 1) run on a staging snapshot first to catch NULLs, 2) enable a migration audit log entry for each user mapping: event=role_mapped old_role=new_role. Ops, can audit retention handle this burst?

ops-bot: @maria scheduled job 'rbac-canonical-backfill' queued for 2024-03-22T22:00:00Z. Estimated duration: 8-12 minutes in staging.

josh: Oncall will be online at 21:30 UTC. I'll monitor for error spikes and permission-denied regressions. Can we add a quick smoke checklist?

maria: Smoke checklist (short):
- Verify admin endpoints (create org, user invite) succeed for admin accounts.
- Verify service automation tokens retain 'service' mapping.
- Spot-check 50 random users for non-null canonical_role.
- Confirm audit events written to auditdb with event=role_mapped.
- Run quick e2e on signup path to ensure default role assignment.

kevin: Noted. I found a staging run earlier where ~0.3% of service accounts got canonical_role=NULL because the role name didn't match patterns (older services). That caused automation to drop to viewer and integrations broke. We should backfill by user.flag_service = true -> 'service' before finalizing.

alyssa: Good catch. Add this pre-step to migration:

```sql
UPDATE roles r SET canonical_role = 'service'
FROM users u
WHERE r.id = u.role_id AND u.service_account = true AND r.canonical_role IS NULL;
```

maria: We'll add idempotency and prechecks: migration acquires a named lock, writes progress to migration_jobs table, and is safe to re-run. Also will create a rollback plan: restore from pre-migration snapshot and a role-mapping backup encrypted with KMS key 'redwood-rbac-enc'.

samir: On KMS: confirm ops will encrypt the backup and that key policy allows restore in prod-only. Also need a KMS access audit for the migration operator.

ops-bot: Backup encryption job completed and stored at s3://redwood-backups/rbac/migration-20240322.enc (kms-key: redwood-rbac-enc). Access: ops, security-admin only.

josh: During the staging run, we saw one unexpected behavior: tokens issued before migration still use old role string in token claims. Some downstream services read the old claim name. We need a compatibility shim: token verifier should accept old_role OR canonical_role for 7 days post-migration.

maria: Agreed. Add a temporary compatibility layer in the token validation service and in the tracing filters, annotated with feature-flag 'rbac-compat-202403'. We'll remove after 7 days and after we confirm no 403 spikes.

kevin: Any customer-impacting risk? If someone had custom RBAC rules relying on old strings, their permissions may change. We should send a short heads-up to accounts with >100 seats and RBAC custom rules. Customer success to own comms.

maria: Action items:
- @alyssa: run full staging migration tonight and verify smoke checklist.
- @josh: monitor and be ready to rollback to snapshot.
- @kevin: deploy compatibility shim and add metric for 'rbac_claim_mismatch'.
- @samir: prepare communication template for impacted customers and coordinate CS.
- @maria: run prod canary 02:00 UTC, then 4-hour observation before wider rollout.

samir: I'll draft the email and include recommended remediation steps for customers that hit regressions.

ops-bot: Staging run started at 2024-03-22T22:01:12Z. Job id: rb-20240322-stg-01.

maria: Staging run result: found the earlier service-account mismatch but pre-step fixed it. No critical failures. Two minor audit write latency spikes (50–80ms extra) — within acceptable range.

josh: I'm seeing a single downstream service that still rejects tokens due to caching of old role->permission matrix. Flushed cache, now OK. Note: add cache-warm step post-migration.

kevin: After canary, plan to run backfills in throttled batches across regions to limit DB contention. Also enabling migration_job entries for traceability.

maria: Prod canary scheduled at 02:00 UTC. I'll post an update in #incidents if anything goes wrong. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
